summary:
Held 2 of today's 10 biggest US movers.

• 4 upside misses — SNDK +15%, KLAC +13%, AMAT +11%, SATS +11%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (PTC -12%, ADBE -9%, ORCL -9%, AKAM -7%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: SNDK (+14.66%) — Q3 FY2026 earnings beat (revenue +251% YoY, EPS $24.43 vs prior-year loss) combined with Morgan Stanley upgrade citing a prolonged AI NAND upcycle; Susquehanna PT raised to $3,250. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe. SNDK trades at ~$1,883/share (+693% YTD), likely breaching nominal-price and RSI ceilings in all universe screens; the 14%+ gap crystallised from post-earnings institutional buying that requires pre-open positioning ahead of any intraday signal window.

top_movers.catalyst: Q4 FY2026 EPS $4.37 beat estimates by 31.6% ($3.32 est); revenue +14% to $4.57B; $1B buyback authorized and quarterly dividend raised 14% — pre-market release June 9.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe (mid-cap convenience-store/fuel retail). news-reactive-disclosure flagged the catalyst but the ~20% pre-market gap likely tripped its max-gap entry filter, leaving no actionable opening-session setup.
top_movers.suggestion: In news-reactive-disclosure, add a pre-open entry path for EPS beats ≥25%: allow limit orders at T-30 min if gap <+12% and pre-market volume ≥2× 30-day avg, sized at 0.3× normal — current hard gap cap misses extreme-beat continuation.

top_movers.catalyst: Q3 FY2026 earnings beat (revenue +251% YoY, EPS $24.43 vs prior-year loss) combined with Morgan Stanley upgrade citing a prolonged AI NAND upcycle; Susquehanna PT raised to $3,250.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. SNDK trades at ~$1,883/share (+693% YTD), likely breaching nominal-price and RSI ceilings in all universe screens; the 14%+ gap crystallised from post-earnings institutional buying that requires pre-open positioning ahead of any intraday signal window.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a post-earnings gap sleeve: admit names with ≥+10% open gap on a revenue-beat quarter regardless of nominal-price ceiling, capped at a 1-day holding period and 0.5× normal position size, to capture asymmetric earnings-momentum moves like this one.

top_movers.catalyst: KLAC's 10-for-1 stock split began trading on an adjusted basis June 12, amplified by a Q3 FY2026 revenue beat ($3.41B) and raised FY guidance on AI-driven process-control demand, plus a 21% dividend hike and fresh analyst upgrades (Cantor Fitzgerald PT $2,500).
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — pre-split KLAC traded above $21,000/share, far above any practical per-share price ceiling in the screener. The universe was compiled on pre-split prices so the newly accessible ~$2,400 name was never evaluated; the earnings/split catalyst also required overnight positioning bef
top_movers.suggestion: Add a post-split ingestion rule that re-screens split-effective-date names against all universe filters using split-adjusted prices at market open, so gap-momentum strategies can evaluate day-one moves for names that have crossed into tradeable price ranges.

top_movers.catalyst: Applied Materials Q2 2026 earnings beat: revenue $7.91B and EPS $2.86 topped estimates; raised CY2026 semiconductor equipment growth outlook to >30%, plus Barclays PT lift to $590.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — AMAT is a mega-cap semiconductor-equipment name (~$450B market cap) whose +11% move was an overnight post-earnings gap. Reactive intraday signals cannot pre-position before the open when the print drops after prior-day close.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a large-cap semis-equipment tier (AMAT, KLAC, LRCX) with a post-earnings gap-gate: if open/prev-close ≥ +5% and earnings were reported <16h prior, allow entry on first 30-min breakout confirmation rather than requiring prior-session volume signal.

top_movers.catalyst: FCC approved EchoStar's $40B spectrum sale — SpaceX acquires 65 MHz for $17B, AT&T acquires 50 MHz for $23B; SATS's ~2.2% SpaceX stake further amplified the rally as a SpaceX IPO proxy.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — SATS is a mid-cap satellite/telecom name outside standard screens. The +11% move was a regulatory catalyst (FCC spectrum ruling) requiring pre-open positioning before any technical or momentum signal could fire.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a regulatory-event watch list for FCC spectrum/M&A decision candidates; the news-reactive strategy should auto-include these names and trigger on ≥3× avg volume gap-up within 15 min of open when a ruling drops.

top_movers.catalyst: Post-Q2 FY2026 selloff extended as analysts (Citi, Berenberg) cut targets after CFO confirmed new ARR ex-deferred was ~flat YoY, exposing weak organic growth behind headline beats.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. PTC is a large-cap PLM/IoT software name; the drop is a multi-week post-earnings drift on ARR-quality concerns, not an intraday gap event — momentum and news-reactive screens would not trigger.
top_movers.suggestion: (no actionable change — capturing multi-week post-earnings ARR-quality drift on an out-of-universe name requires a fundamental-drift sleeve or short capability; neither fits current risk tolerance without significant scope expansion)

top_movers.catalyst: Q2 beat ($6.62B rev vs $6.46B est, non-GAAP EPS $5.96 vs $5.82) was overshadowed by CFO Dan Durn's surprise departure, a freemium pivot delaying Creative Cloud price hikes, and an Evercore ISI downgrade (Outperform→In Line, PT $325→$225).
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — ADBE is a large-cap SaaS name (~$95B market cap). The -9% move was a post-earnings gap triggered after June 11 close; no intraday technical or momentum signal could front-run it without a dedicated earnings-reaction playbook.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a post-earnings gap-down rule: if earnings-day open gaps ≥-5% versus prior close and first-30-min volume ≥1.5× 20-day avg, flag for a short entry sized to sector-risk limits — this would have caught ADBE at open without pre-positioning risk.

top_movers.catalyst: Q4 FY2026 earnings beat (EPS $2.11 vs $1.95 est, revenue +21% to $19.2B) but stock sold off on surprise $40B AI capex plan, raising concerns about debt load and free-cash-flow sustainability.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — ORCL is a $500B+ mega-cap cloud/enterprise name. Additionally, the move was a post-earnings gap reaction (results reported June 10 after close); capturing it required either a pre-positioned short into the print or a news-reactive entry at the open, both outside current strategy
top_movers.suggestion: Add a post-earnings capex-shock screen: if a name beats EPS but guides capex ≥20% above prior consensus, flag it for a gap-fade short entry within 15 min of open — requires enabling short capability for large-cap tech in at least one strategy.

top_movers.catalyst: Continued unwind of May AI-contract surge ($110→$165 peak); selling accelerates on CDN sector rotation, $3.5B convertible-note dilution overhang, and elevated-capex margin concerns; no single discrete June 12 newsbreak found.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. AKAM is a ~$19B large-cap CDN/cloud-security name not covered by existing sleeves. The move is a post-hype downtrend continuation requiring short exposure — outside standard long-only momentum or mean-reversion parameters.
top_movers.suggestion: (no actionable change — outside risk tolerance / requires short capability we don't have); if a large-cap short-momentum sleeve is ever added, AKAM-type setups (≥20% off 30-day peak + convertible-note overhang) would be natural entry candidates.
